findings.actual_full_rebuild_trigger: Unchanged p8_scale.rs:897 executes build(true) for each full_control; unchanged build_plan.rs:319-336 stages any full mode through write_full_snapshot_build_staging. Shared snapshot contents now opts in at line111. The WAL staging owner creates FULL_SCHEMA_SQL, drops only secondary indexes, and invokes the closure inside an actual transaction, matching the canonical fast-path requirements. This affects nonempty formal full controls regardless of the fixture's zero test-file population. Actual speedup is not established by this static call trace.
findings.schema_gate: Autocommit and any TEMP object retain the original path. The complete ordered main.sqlite_schema type/name/tbl_name/sql set, excluding indexes only, must equal a fresh schema instantiated using this linked SQLite library. Unexpected tables, views, triggers and changed FK/schema definitions fall back. Reference/schema query failures propagate, never silently authorize the fast path.
findings.survivors_and_order: Each maximum-256-file window records actual files and literal_index rowid maxima. The base file INSERT and literal INSERT OR IGNORE remain unchanged and retain their original ordering. Flush copies actual new base rows in (before,after] ordered by rowid, so ignored duplicates are not mirrored and cross-window literals belonging to an earlier file are retained. All attempted literal rows count conservatively toward capacity. Checked count conversion/addition and after<i64::MAX avoid SQLite's random-rowid allocation path; otherwise the unchanged per-row path is used.
findings.fts_scope: Only files_fts and literal_fts are delayed. files/path trigger, symbols/FTS trigger, chunks and uncompressed chunks_fts, document/identity writes and all leaf binders stay in their original positions. Configuration units, metadata and final graph-signature baseline remain after the completed mirror windows.
findings.failure_boundary: Any base-write or flush error exits the new method immediately. It does not own or roll back the borrowed transaction. The unchanged WAL temp owner propagates write_fn failure, closes/removes the failed temp database and cannot return a generation floor. The unchanged rebuild protocol calls swap only after build succeeds. In the DirectWriter OFF path, write_fn? also prevents commit/recreate/restore/swap, but this is abandonment and non-publication, NOT a physical rollback guarantee for the failed temp file. Public write_file_data remains available with its original partial-state semantics.
findings.resource_and_performance_scope: Window bound is 256 files, not a byte bound or SQLite RSS bound. No new row-vector copy is introduced; base write units already exist. Two FTS INSERT SELECT calls replace per-file/per-literal mirror executions, with rowid ranges and MAX tail lookup; total FTS token work still occurs. Statement-count controls establish fewer statement runs, not measured 100k speedup or the cause of old E failures.
